primitives.verbatim_quote: Can we build a 239-problem benchmark across four scientific domains that (a) transforms known physical models into unfamiliar mathematical representations (LSR-Transform) and (b) introduces synthetic discovery-driven problems with novel terms (LSR-Synth), and do current LLM-based methods actually discover — or merely recite?

reasoning_traces.think:
The LLM-SRBench benchmark introduces two core paradigms: LSR-Transform and LSR-Synth. LSR-Transform rewrites known physical laws into less familiar mathematical forms, thereby blocking memorization and forcing symbolic reasoning. This is achieved by mapping existing models into alternate representations such that their structure remains invariant but their appearance is altered. LSR-Synth generates entirely new equations with synthetic terms, validated via numerical solvers to ensure physical consistency. These synthetic problems demand data-driven inference rather than rote recall. The benchmark evaluates systems using symbolic accuracy metrics like exact-structure match rate and NMSE, distinguishing between numeric fit and true discovery. Memorization diagnosis uses error-curve analysis to differentiate recitation (sharp drop-offs) from genuine search (gradual decay). Complexity is controlled via expression-tree node count, ensuring fair comparisons. The validation strategy includes ID vs OOD NMSE comparisons and ablation studies of DataBlind baselines to isolate the necessity of data. This dual approach ensures that models must reason rather than simply reproduce known equations.
